additionalAttacksRunBeyondThePromptList.attack: The claim that R-6 and R-10 are 'leftover beyond OBL-FX-AUTHORING's fourteen FX classes' is false because some FX class already supplies them
additionalAttacksRunBeyondThePromptList.evidence: OBL-FX-AUTHORING in permission-leftover-join.v2 is scoped by namedClassesNotAuthored to exactly the fourteen FX ids; R-6 and R-10 are raceSemantics races, not FX classes. Tested the nearest candidate: FX-4 crashes at every journal write and fsync boundary for L-1..L-8, and L-7 IS CLEANUP-CLOSED (CLN), so FX-4's crash points do touch cleanup. But FX-4's five assertions are all journal-ordering — exactly one total order, no duplicate sequence number, no renumbered gap, no *-INTENT without a terminal outcome or INDETERMINATE, no effect initiated whose intent record is absent. None asserts that cleanup re-runs, that the bound is re-measured from recovery, or that exhaustion journals a residual rather than looping. R-6 is moreover death MID-cleanup rather than at a journal boundary, so FX-4 does not even pin the crash point. For R-10, no FX class delivers an expiry: FX-5 is the four revocation positions and FX-7 re-runs FX-4 and FX-5 under clock perturbation, so neither exercises an expiry.

whyThisPassesTheStandardThatFailedItsSib: Three tests governed the truncation findings cited by this artifact. (1) Is the carried quotation equal to live source? Here all four strings are == equal, at the exact lengths the dispatch names. (2) Does anything in the source fail to survive into the artifact? Live v9 race objects carry exactly four keys and all four are carried, twice — once in basedOn and once in the initialStates entry — so nothing is left behind. (3) Is the shortfall excused as house convention? No shortfall exists to excuse; the house standard set by permission-fx4-input-corpus.v1 and permission-fx5-input-corpus.v2 is complete carry, and this meets it and adds whyDeterministic, which v1 lacked entirely. The derived fields — boundMeasuredFrom 'recovery', exhaustion 'journals a residual rather than looping', materializedAs, behavesAs, evaluatedByWallClockNow false — were each checked against the outcome text they derive from and none misstates it.
notCharged: The artifact carries no explicit 'Does not claim QUALIFIED' line, unlike some siblings. Nothing in it claims QUALIFIED, so the attack fails on the facts; this is an absent belt-and-braces line, not a defect. Graded identically to the same observation on permission-fx12-input-corpus.v1.

R-6 and R-10 are named as leftover beyond OBL-FX-AUTHORING without an obligation code being minted for them. The artifact correctly declines to mint one — obligation codes are the leftover-join's to assign, and that join is frozen at D-163 — and it does not claim any existing code covers them. A later join revision is the place for that; requiring it here would be this reviewer legislating rather than measuring.

verdictStatement: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. Custody holds on every axis: the subject is unmoved at 7b93dc3e… across start and end measurements, v1 is unmoved at 300f3f7d… and 0444, the version number is not reused, all five cited digests match, HEAD and required-now are unchanged, and no journal bytes, expiry-age or cleanup-bound number is authored anywhere. The dispatch's four character-exact assertions were tested by == and all four pass — R-6 race+outcome at 281 of 281, R-10 at 445 of 445, and both whyDeterministic strings equal — and the same four strings are carried a second time inside the initialStates entries and are equal there too. Live v9 race objects have exactly four keys and the subject carries all four for both races, so completeness is structural rather than a matter of judgement, and the truncation class that this artifact's v1 shared with CLAUDE-FX5-SF1 and CLAUDE-FX6-SF1 is repaired by the remedy those findings prescribed. I attempted five refutations beyond the dispatch list — that an FX class already supplies R-6 or R-10, that an entry is missing as in the FX-12 corpus, that v2 regressed v1, that the g09v3 citation misstates a verdict, and that the lands field claims a kinship it does not have — and every one failed against live bytes.
